pattern: Two things the rest of the catalogue should be checked against. (1) The doc's trailing extras follow Dropout's own ordering of the season collection: data/dropout-collections.yaml lists `dimension-20-escape-from-the-bloodkeep` as episodes 1-6, then `escape-from-the-bloodkeep-behind-the-scenes`, then the two reunions (itemIds 497564..514667, 517277, 518360, 538040, ascending), episode 6's `upNextIds` is [517277, 518360, 538040] in that order, and the Dropout channel's members playlist PLuKg-WhduhkmhsvbPmu7MCWzKCFfeRrve titles the BTS "| Escape from the Bloodkeep | Ep. 7". The file's order (BTS, Reunion 1, Reunion 2) matches it; it is the date that does not. (2) The date artefact: a `bts:` whose Dropout page carries no `releaseDate` and whose `published:` equals a members upload shared by five or more entries of its season (release-date.ts's BULK_MEMBERS batch rule) is dated by a backfill, not a release. A sweep of every Dimension 20 `bts:` with a dateless Dropout page found the Bloodkeep BTS to be the only one in that state (seven entries share 2019-09-10; the Unsleeping City per-cast BTS videos also equal their members uploads but in groups of three, which dates.md already says are "usually within a day or two" of release); the same sweep should run over every show. Where that happens, Dropout's `itemId` is a usable instrument the model does not yet exploit: itemIds are monotonic in page creation, and bracketing an undated page between TVDB- or Dropout-dated neighbours in data/dropout.yaml dates it to within a few days (here 516658 and 517667 are both 2019-06-10, 518413 is 2019-06-12, and the BTS is 517277). `verify-dates --unmatched` could print that bracket for every page with no catalogue date, and `verify-playlists --order` could compare a season's extras order with the collection's `episodes` list the way it already does with YouTube playlists.

verdicts.evidence: The BTS's `published: 2019-09-10` is its members upload and nothing else: data/videos/dropout.yaml has rqwcG_2upgk uploadedAt 2019-09-10T23:23:58Z, publishedAt 2019-09-10T23:27:19Z, in the same two-hour batch as all six episodes' members uploads (gmbEkxuo6h0 21:26 through XCcHTrZR0bE 22:03), all seven added to Dropout's playlist on 2019-09-12. The six episodes were re-dated to Dropout's releases (2019-04-30 to 06-04, Tuesdays; TVDB agrees) but the BTS kept the upload date it had when the entry was first written (commit 9b5d50c, 2024-03-07, when the finale was still dated 2020-04-04), because Dropout's page carries no date (scraped releaseDate null; fetched today, no date on the page), TVDB's Dimension 20 season 2 lists only the six episodes, TVmaze with specials included has no entry, and the D20 wiki is blocked at the proxy (403), so it was not looked at. Seven entries sharing one members date is a backfill batch by the project's own BULK_MEMBERS=5 rule. Dropout orders the BTS before both reunions (collection `episodes` list; episode 6's upNextIds [517277, 518360, 538040]; members playlist title "Ep. 7"), and its itemId 517277 sits between pages TVDB dates to 2019-06-10 (516658 Troopers BTS, 517667 Kingpin Katie "Going Clean") and 2019-06-12 (518413 Cartoon Hell), and ahead of Reunion Pt 1's 518360 (2019-06-26, TVDB and the free upload RGb2VYNd4ws agree). The reunions' dates are sound: TVDB 2019-06-26 and 2019-07-10, free uploads on the Dimension 20 channel the same days. So the BTS was released the week after the 2019-06-04 finale -- the show ran Tuesdays, so most probably 2019-06-11 (bracket 06-10 to 06-12; Troopers' BTS followed its own finale by exactly a week the same month). With that date the file order BTS, Reunion 1, Reunion 2 is release order and matches Dropout's; moving the BTS behind Cast Reunion (Part 2) instead would break Dropout's order on the strength of a date the project's rules already reject.
verdicts.proposal: The BTS's date: `published: 2019-09-10` on `bts: Behind the Scenes` (dropout: escape-from-the-bloodkeep-behind-the-scenes) is probably 2019-06-11 (certainly between 2019-06-10 and 06-12, and before 06-26); source: Dropout's collection order and "Ep. 7" numbering, the itemId bracket against TVDB-dated neighbours, and the Tuesday cadence. Record it as a `[release-dates]` override in config/dropout.toml with that evidence beside it (or as a cadence-set date with a comment, as Unsleeping City 2 episode 8 is), and leave the file order as it stands.

# Dimension 20 / Fantasy High (Chapter 1): order audit

File: /home/user/youtube/curation/seasons.yaml, lines 11-159. No comment block above `show:` beyond the file header; the only in-doc comment is on the 2024 minis auction (lines 155-156). Dropout's pages for every entry in this doc carry no `releaseDate` (`verify-dates --show="Dimension 20" --unmatched` lists all of them as "rests on curated"), so `verify-dates` has no opinion on any date here.

## What the four inverted entries are

The four `bts:` entries are the four episodes of Dropout's show "Fantasy High: Extra Credit" (collection `fantasy-high-extra-credit`, data/dropout.yaml, data/dropout-collections.yaml line 3687: "After the final bell, game master Brennan Lee Mulligan chats with your favorite cast & crew members"). Dropout's descriptions name what each recaps:

- `Wally and Gilear in the Morning with Emily, Murph, and Michael` (Extra Credit ep. 1): "recap episodes 9 & 10" -- filed after episode 10.
- `Parties are Weird but Friendship is Dope with Lou and Rick` (ep. 2): "recap episodes 11 & 12" -- filed after episode 12.
- `Problem Players and Troublesome Tangents with Ally and Zac` (ep. 3): "recap episodes 13 & 14" -- filed after episode 14.
- `The Greatest Nat 20 of All Time with Siobhan and Lou` (ep. 4): "recap episodes 15 & 16" -- filed after episode 17, i.e. after both halves of the Prompocalypse two-parter rather than between them, and so ahead of `Behind the Scenes` (2018-12-27, the finale's making-of).

So every one of the four inversions is the same displaced block: recaps interleaved beside the episode pairs they discuss, nine to ten months after those episodes aired.

## Verdict on the order: deliberate, recorded in git, not in the file

Commit 17e4c5e (2026-09-05, "Link the Fantasy High: Extra Credit recaps to their Dropout pages") states: "The four Extra Credit episodes -- the Fantasy High season 1 recap show, and the ancestor of Adventuring Party -- have been curated all along, as bts entries inside Fantasy High (Chapter 1), interleaved between the episodes each one recaps. [...] No entry moves and none is added or removed." The entries themselves date from the initial import (9b5d50c, 2024-03-07) in these positions.

This is the animation rule (rule 3, "beside the moment they depict") applied to recap talkbacks, and it reads better than the alternative: in strict release order all four would sit together after `Live in Austin` (2019-07-17) and before the 2024 minis auction, a run of four recaps of episodes 9-16 stranded behind the finale, the making-of and two live shows. Dropout's own playlists give no position for them within the season either way: the Dropout channel's "Dimension 20: Fantasy High (Full Episodes)" (20 entries) carries no recap and has `Behind the Scenes` at position 17 titled "Ep. 18"; the recaps live only in "Fantasy High: Extra Credit (Full Episodes)" (Dropout channel) and "Dimension 20: Extra Credits" (dimension20show channel), both four entries. The interleave is our editorial choice, and Dropout's ordering is not evidence against it.

By the letter of rule 4 the exception is undocumented: the file carries no comment. Recommendation: do not reorder; add a comment above `Wally and Gilear in the Morning` saying the four Extra Credit recaps sit after the episode pair each one recaps (after Part 2 of Prompocalypse for the last), out of date order by design, as Dropout's descriptions name the episodes.

## The dates are wrong, and fixing them does not remove the inversions

All four `published:` dates (2019-09-27, 2019-09-28, 2019-10-04, 2019-10-05) are the dimension20show free-upload dates (`Recapping Fantasy High with ...`, data/videos/dimension20show.yaml, publishedAt 2019-09-27T17:30, 09-28T17:30, 10-04T17:30, 10-05T17:30). Dropout released the show earlier, weekly on Wednesdays:

- TheTVDB (Dimension 20 specials, https://thetvdb.com/series/dimension-20/seasons/official/0): Wally and Gilear in the Morning 2019-08-28; Parties Are Weird But Friendship is Dope 2019-09-04; Problem Players & Troublesome Tangents 2019-09-11; The Greatest Nat 20 Of All Time 2019-09-18.
- Independent corroboration from Dropout's own `itemId`s, which Vimeo OTT issues in creation order. Each recap's id falls between the ids of consecutive weekly Unsleeping City episodes whose dates are curated and Dropout-verified: 589470 (Wally) between subway-skirmish 587026 (2019-08-27) and borough-of-dreams 589980 (2019-09-03); 594498 (Parties) between borough-of-dreams and panic-at-the-art-show 595793 (2019-09-10); 600304 (Problem Players) between that and home-for-the-holidays 602236 (2019-09-17); 604737 (Nat 20) between that and broadway-brawl 609452 (2019-09-24). Four consecutive weeks, exactly TVDB's.
- The Dropout channel's members uploads of all four landed in one batch on 2019-09-18 (17:54-18:09 UTC), the day of the fourth's release -- the complete set uploaded once it was finished, which fits the weekly run and rules out the public uploads being first availability.

Under the project's date rule (first availability; Dropout's release for members content; a public YouTube upload only where it predates Dropout) the four dates should be 2019-08-28, 2019-09-04, 2019-09-11 and 2019-09-18. Since Dropout's pages carry no `releaseDate`, the place to record them so `verify-dates` keeps enforcing them is data/tvdb-dates.yaml, which currently has no `Dimension 20:` table; its convention is to key by curated show name then TVDB's episode title, and the lookup is by normalised title, so check that the entries' titles (which carry a "with X and Y" suffix TVDB's do not) still match, or key by the entry titles. TVDB is not uniformly reliable for this show -- it dates `Fantasy High: Behind the Scenes` 2018-07-10, before the season premiered, a placeholder -- so only the four corroborated dates should be adopted. The itemId check is the kind of cadence evidence CLAUDE.md asks for and could be reused wherever a Dropout page has no date.

Corrected, the recaps still sit eight to nine months after the episodes they follow, so the inversions remain and the ordering verdict above stands on its own.

## Not wrong, for the record

`Behind the Scenes` 2018-12-27 is first availability: public part 1 (JnAZ4wc0zeM "The Making of Fantasy High") went up 2018-12-27, part 2 (O4jDmG3z8Rg) 2019-01-03, and the members copy is a 2019-09-20 backfill titled "Ep. 18". `Live in Brooklyn` 2019-06-24 and `Live in Austin` 2019-07-17 agree with TVDB.

## Pattern for the rest of the catalogue

Companion `bts:` entries that discuss specific episodes are filed beside those episodes, straight after the last one they cover (after Part 2 when the last is a two-parter's Part 1), regardless of release date. Everywhere else in the catalogue the same placement happens to be date order, because Adventuring Party-style talkbacks air the week of their episode: of the 254 `talkback: true` entries across 25 Dimension 20 docs, none breaks date order except through an `animation:` neighbour or in a handful of rows that other docs' audits will be judging (Crown of Candy talkbacks dated the day before the episode they follow, from `Soft Hugs` on; Pirates of Leviathan `The Buccaneer Buddies Reunite`; Starstruck `No Middle Sliders`; Court of Fey `The Wish Factory`; Mentopolis `Bit City USA`; and Fantasy High (Chapter 2)'s `Fireside Chat with Brennan & Friends` Parts 1-2, dated 2020-03-24/31 after episode 20 dated 2020-04-07). Each should be judged by the same test: which episodes does Dropout's description say it discusses, and does it sit right after them.

## Data-model suggestion (the relayed request invited it)

The placement here is a fact about the entry, not about the order: the recap is *about* episodes 9 and 10. A field naming that -- e.g. `recaps: [9, 10]` on a `bts:` entry, taking Dropout's wording as the source -- would record the exception in the file where rule 4 wants it, machine-readably rather than as a prose comment; let the order audit exempt such entries the way it already exempts `animation:`; and let `aggregate` or `verify-playlists` check that the entry sits after the last episode it names. All four values are given verbatim by Dropout's descriptions.
pattern: Companion bts entries that discuss specific episodes are filed beside those episodes, straight after the last one they cover (after Part 2 when that is a two-parter's Part 1), regardless of release date -- the animation rule applied to recaps/talkbacks, with Dropout's description naming the episodes. In every other D20 doc this coincides with date order because talkbacks air the week of their episode; check the rows where it does not (Crown of Candy talkbacks from Soft Hugs on, Pirates of Leviathan Buccaneer Buddies Reunite, Starstruck No Middle Sliders, Court of Fey The Wish Factory, Mentopolis Bit City USA, Fantasy High (Chapter 2) Fireside Chat Parts 1-2) by the same test: which episodes does Dropout say it discusses, and does it sit right after them. Separately: for entries whose Dropout page carries no releaseDate, Dropout itemIds are issued in creation order and bracket a release to the week when read against dated neighbours.
